require "csv"

# Returns the five CSV rows with the highest numeric value in +column+.
# The CSV is expected to have a header row; +column+ can be a header name
# or a header index. Rows are returned as CSV::Row objects.
def top_rows(path, column)
  rows = CSV.read(path, headers: true).each_with_index.map do |row, index|
    value = Float(row[column])
    [value, index, row]
  end

  rows.sort_by { |value, index, _row| [-value, index] }
      .first(5)
      .map(&:last)
end
